newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices sharply lower in week.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices sharply lower in week.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were sharply lower than last week in quiet Wednesday trade as temperatures remained above normal in key regions keeping a tight lid on demand.
Traders expected more of the same for the rest of the week as continued mild weather was forecast for western Canada at least through Sunday.

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.45/1.50 per gigajoule, down from C$1.75/1.80 last week. AECO gas for March delivery was quoted at C$1.53/1.54 per GJ, a drop from C$1.85 a week ago.
"There's an ocean of gas for sale at C$1.50 and buyers are hanging for C$1.45," a Calgary-based marketer said.

He said any premium once associated with fears over low storage volumes in the west had disappeared. "We could take out a (billion cubic feet) per day until the end of March and still not hit the cushion. Storage is in great shape," he said, adding that the ample stocks could mean lower summer prices.

At the borders, prices at Sumas remained soft despite the easing of transport contraints on Northwest Pipeline, again thanks to warmer weather in British Columbia and the U.S. Pacific Northwest. Sumas gas was talked in the high US$1.20s per million British thermal units, down from US$1.90 last week.
Niagara was quoted at US$2.15/2.80 per mmBtu, down nearly 50 cents from February 12.
